Meta.title: Gillian Delvigne · Full-stack Developer
Meta.description: A learning engineer turned full-stack developer in Belgium. React, TypeScript, Node, PostgreSQL. Applications built to be understood by the people who use them.

featured.title: From learning simulation to ERP
featured.body: From a simulation where I barely had a finger in the code to Odoo modules where I'm in up to my neck.

items.title: UNamur and Van In/De Boeck
items.body: From 2011, teaching advisor and assistant at UNamur, then editorial assistant and ICT manager at Van In/De Boeck until 2017, where development became part of my job.

items.title: Belgian Red Cross
items.body: Digital Learning Manager until 2021: First aid on the road, the course every driving-licence candidate in Brussels takes (13 modules), and a first-aid app that passed 25,000 users, from specifications to rollout.

items.title: ULB and CPFB
items.body: Learning technologist until 2023: member of the ULB teaching support centre, Moodle and Microsoft Azure administrator at CPFB, where I helped trainers through their digital transition.

items.title: 42 Belgium
items.body: Since 2023, in C and C++ (a curriculum equivalent to a bachelor's in computer science); that is where I wrote minishell, a UNIX shell, and fdf, a 3D wireframe renderer.

items.title: Technobel
items.body: The intensive Odoo Developer track, completed in October 2026 (about 400 hours, 15 places, by admission test): Python, PostgreSQL, ORM, application security.

items.title: Odoo showcase
items.body: In progress on my server (VPS); it will be the next case study.

Difficulty.title: What this project demanded
Difficulty.intro: Six criteria, from 0 to 4: the further a branch reaches, the more the project demanded on that point.

definitions.scope: How many different pieces have to work together? (a website, a server, a database, outside services)
definitions.coupling: How many parties, human or technical, must the project keep in agreement? When one changes, the others have to follow (on the code side: APIs, connected services; on the organisation side: departments, partners, the client)
definitions.stakes: What happens when it breaks? (a minor annoyance, lost money, exposed data)
definitions.conformance: Does the result have to reproduce an imposed model exactly? (a specification, a standard, an existing program)
definitions.rules: How many business rules does the project have to apply? (exceptions, special cases, specific requirements, branching paths)
definitions.disciplines: How many different hats did the project require? (frontend development, backend development, design, writing, teaching)

3.name: High
3.detail: several elements that depend on one another

4.name: Very high
4.detail: everything is linked, an error spreads
